title: A Theoretical Analysis of Why Masked Diffusion Models Mitigate the Reversal Curse
abstract: arXiv:2602.02133v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Autoregressive language models (ARMs) suffer from the reversal curse: after learning ''$A$ is $B$,'' they often fail on the reverse query ''$B$ is $A$.'' Masked diffusion language models (MDMs) exhibit this failure in a much weaker form, but the underlying reason has remained unclear. A common explanation attributes this mitigation to their any-order masked training objective. However, observing ''$[\mathbf{M}]$ is $B$'' during training teaches recovery of $A$ from $B$ in one positional configuration, and does not by itself explain why the learned evidence should transfer to the reverse prompt ''$B$ is $[\mathbf{M}]$.'' We provide a theoretical analysis showing that this transfer arises from a parameter-level coupling between forward and reverse positional conditionals: shared Transformer parameters store token-pair evidence, while relative positional encodings route attention through queries and keys without changing the value

translated_title: 掩码扩散模型为何能缓解反转诅咒的理论分析
translated_abstract: 自回归语言模型（ARMs）存在“反转诅咒”问题：在学到“A是B”之后，它们在回答反向查询“B是A”时往往会失败。掩码扩散语言模型（MDMs）以弱得多的形式表现出这种失败，但其背后的根本原因一直不清楚。一种常见的解释将这种缓解归因于其任意顺序的掩码训练目标。然而，在训练中观察到“[M]是B”只能教会模型在一种位置配置下从B恢复A，这本身并不能解释为什么学到的证据能够迁移到反向提示“B是[M]”。我们提供了理论分析，表明这种迁移源于正向与反向位置条件分布之间的参数级耦合：共享的Transformer参数存储词元对的证据，而相对位置编码通过查询和键引导注意力，而不改变值本身。
tldr: 该论文通过理论分析证明，掩码扩散模型缓解反转诅咒的原因在于正向与反向位置条件分布之间存在参数级耦合——共享的Transformer参数存储词元对证据，而相对位置编码在不改变值的情况下引导注意力，从而使学到的证据能够迁移到反向提示。
en_tdlr: This paper theoretically demonstrates that masked diffusion models mitigate the reversal curse through a parameter-level coupling between forward and reverse positional conditionals, where shared Transformer parameters store token-pair evidence while relative positional encodings route attention without altering the values.
